knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What is deviance in a GLM? (2) What does scaled deviance involve? (3) What is being estimated? (4) Name one reason model choice is not today's LO.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Deviance compares fitted vs saturated likelihoods; scaled deviance divides by scale. Parameters of the GLM are estimated. Nested model choice is tomorrow.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) In one sentence each, what are deviance and scaled deviance, and what estimation principle is typically used for GLM parameters? (2) Refuse: 'Deleting insignificant terms until p-values look nice finishes explaining deviance and GLM estimation.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Deviance compares the fitted model's log-likelihood to a saturated model (2{ℓ_sat − ℓ_model}); scaled deviance divides by the dispersion/scale when relevant. Parameters are typically estimated by maximum likelihood (often via IWLS). (2) Refuse: mechanical p-value chopping is model-choice behaviour, not the definition or estimation of deviance.
